title: Root-end surgery (removal of a tooth cyst)
what: Through a small cut in the gum, the surgeon removes the tip of the tooth root along with the cyst. The tooth itself stays.
why: When there is a cyst or inflammation at the tip of the root and re-treating the root canals does not work.
duration: the operation usually takes 30 to 90 minutes
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners, as the doctor will say what to stop and when
Allergies, especially to painkillers and antibiotics

prepare.title: X-rays
prepare.text: A 3D scan of the tooth is usually needed.

prepare.title: Root canals
prepare.text: The tooth's canals are often filled before the operation. Ask your doctor.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Eat 1 to 2 hours before the operation.

steps: The surgeon cuts and lifts the gum over the root
Makes a small window in the bone
Removes the cyst and the tip of the root
Sometimes seals the root from the end
feel: Under numbing, you feel pressure but no pain
Afterward, a swollen cheek and pain for 2 to 3 days, and you are given a painkiller
You may get a bruise on your face
after: Hold a cold pack on your cheek for the first hours, with breaks
Soft, not hot, food for a few days
Do not chew on that side
Do not rinse your mouth hard on the first day
Stitches are usually removed after 1 to 2 weeks
red_flags: Bleeding does not stop when you press on it
A fever over 38°C (100.4°F), or swelling that grows after day 3
Swelling spreads to the neck, or trouble swallowing or breathing: call emergency services

faq.a: Usually yes. The root becomes a bit shorter, but the tooth keeps working.

faq.q: Why not just remove the tooth?
faq.a: Keeping your own tooth is better when possible. Your doctor will say if there is a chance.

reminders.text: Tooth root surgery tomorrow. No alcohol. Eat 1 to 2 hours before the visit. Take your medicines as your doctor said.
